fichas.title: Landscape Architecture: Design Aspects and Concepts
fichas.summary: Landscape design treats built and unbuilt land as related parts of a spatial composition. The page describes horizontal organization through ideas, function, design and form, and vertical elements that reinforce it through materials and spatial context. Compositions may use reference and contrast, superimposition, repetition, structures, lines, material areas, walls, solitary objects, edges, bodies, topography and roofs. Landscape architects should contribute from the start of a project so outdoor spaces form an integrated unit with buildings or town planning. Illustration should suit the design concept and project stage: sketches can communicate preliminary ideas, while detailed design and working drawings emphasize the functional depiction of structures and objects.
uses: Organize outdoor space in relation to its surroundings
Integrate landscape with buildings and town planning
Define space through built or planted vertical elements
Communicate landscape design concepts through drawings and images
